brand.scope: wordmark mark and app icon only

display.purpose: Page H1 only; italic 700 Barlow Condensed, uppercase, +0.01em.

headline.purpose: Page H2 content and dialog titles.

title.purpose: Settings group heads and sign-in card names.

tab.purpose: Tab labels on the Review and Choice coupon heads.

label.purpose: Column heads and the rail's small wordmark line.

row.purpose: Game names in the list; truncates with an ellipsis.

data.purpose: Records a person checks: bundle, year, date, key, time. Tabular figures.

numeral.purpose: Counts in tallies (22px) and tab counts (14px).

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Floating layers only: the unsigned-in coupon and dialogs. Sheets, rows, tabs and inputs have no shadow.

motion.name: stamp-in
motion.purpose: Stamp landing on the Run list only: from rotate(-4deg) scale(1.14) opacity 0 to rotate(-4deg) scale(1). Never in History. Removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: spinner-turn
motion.purpose: Spinner ring. Under reduced motion it becomes a static 6px dot.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; stamps show at their final state instantly.

breakpoints.name: review-columns-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Review columns: From becomes flexible, Note narrows to 170px.

breakpoints.name: history-stack
breakpoints.purpose: History stacks the export card below the table.

radii.name: sm
radii.purpose: Controls, pills, banners, inputs, sheet bottoms.

radii.name: notch
radii.purpose: Coupon heads and the active nav item only (clip-path).

narrative.overview:
Every Humble key is a coupon in a traveller's ticket wallet. The screen shows the whole backlog as a coupon book: each key sits on a ruled sheet, the groups are coupon heads in a row of tabs, and nothing is spent until the person presses Redeem. Once Steam accepts a key, its coupon receives a stamp, and the stamp stays. History is the same stack of stamped coupons, so a key is never lost from view.

The look borrows the type, palette and ruled-coupon construction of a jet-age airline ticket wallet and nothing more. The ground is stock white. Sheets are coupon white, ruled with navy hairlines and broken by dashed tear lines. The rail and primary buttons are carrier navy. Counts, ticks and redeemed stamps are carbon purple. Void red is kept for failure. Density is working density: 44px rows, 15px body, many keys on one screen, because the audience is clearing a backlog. The personality sits in the sheet heads, the notches and the stamp. Body text stays plain for the less confident person.

Dark mode is the same wallet at night: a navy ground, sheets one step lighter, and the carbon and void tones lifted so they stay legible.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled coupon sheets with dashed tear lines; sheets, rows and tabs carry no shadow
Notched corners on tab heads and the active nav item; sheets stay square
Barlow Condensed caps for chrome, Libre Franklin for reading, Courier Prime for data
The stamp is the one signature object, and it marks an outcome
Carrier navy for the rail and primary actions; carbon purple for counts and success; void red for failure
Calm, dense working surfaces with the world carried by rules, notches and stamps

rules.name: The Carbon Means Done Rule
rules.body: Carbon purple marks what was counted or completed: counts, ticks, redeemed stamps and success. Two other carbon uses exist (link hover and the export heading); neither adds a new meaning.

rules.name: The Red Is Failure Rule
rules.body: Void red marks a failed key and its reason, and the danger tone. The danger tone is used only for destructive or irreversible actions (Delete all local data, Reveal and export). Red is never decorative.

rules.name: The Italic Headline Rule
rules.body: Only page H1s are italic. Every H2 and below is upright Barlow caps, so the slant is never a second voice.

rules.name: The Typewriter Data Rule
rules.body: Anything a person checks against their own records (bundle, year, date, key, time, count of attempts) is set in Courier Prime. Names and sentences are never set in it.

rules.name: The Sheet Fills The Window Rule
rules.body: The Review sheet takes the remaining window height and the list scrolls within it. Headers and tabs never scroll away, so the stamp and the Redeem count stay in view on a long backlog.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Sheets, rows, tabs and inputs never cast a shadow. A shadow appears only on a floating layer that sits over the screen.

rules.name: The Tear Line Rule
rules.body: Rows are separated by dashed perforations, never solid lines. A vertical tear line appears only on the Review stub, at 64px.

rules.name: The Notch Rule
rules.body: Only coupon heads (Review tabs and Choice month names) and the active nav item take a cut corner. Sheets, cards, dialogs and buttons stay square so the notch keeps its meaning.

rules.name: The Stamp Is A Result Rule
rules.body: A stamp records a key's outcome or a completed state (added, already owned, error, signed in). A pill marks a note on a key that has not been acted on yet.

rules.name: The Ink-Wear Stamp Rule
rules.body: Every stamp carries the procedural ink-wear mask (src/renderer/assets/stamp-ink.png, generated by scripts/gen-stamp-ink.mjs, applied with mask-image). The mask is the stamp's only texture; the renderer build sets assetsInlineLimit to 0 because the CSP blocks data: images.

rules.name: The One Landing Rule
rules.body: Stamps are the only entrance motion in the system. On the Run list a stamp lands once in 160ms: from rotate(-4deg) scale(1.14) and opacity 0 to rotate(-4deg) scale(1), on a cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) ease. It never runs in History. Reduced motion removes it and every other transition.

rules.name: The Working Screens Rule
rules.body: The world lives in rules, tabs, notches and stamps. Working screens carry no paper grain and no decorative stripes. The only texture on a working screen is the stamp's ink-wear mask. The speed-stripe mark is the wordmark's alone.

dos: Do use Carrier Navy for the one primary action on each screen, and Carbon Purple for counts and success.
Do use a Stamp for a key's outcome, and a Pill for a note on a key that has not been acted on yet.
Do pair every colour with words. A tone is never the only signal; "uses up its gift link" and "won't work" carry the meaning in text.
Do keep rows at 44px with dashed perforations, and keep the Review sheet filling the window with its list scrolling inside it.
Do set counts in Courier Prime bold, and name the cost in plain words before an irreversible action.
Do keep the Stamp double rule and rotation exactly as set (-4deg, 92% opacity); the stamp is the one object that is allowed to tilt.
Do use the danger tone and the typed confirmation for any action that cannot be undone.
donts: Don't add an eyebrow or kicker label above a heading. The surface brief bans it; the headings stand alone.
Don't use italic outside page H1s.
Don't shadow sheets, rows, tabs or inputs. The lift shadow is for floating layers only.
Don't use hard offset shadows; the world is flat rules and soft lift, not a neobrutalist offset.
Don't use Void Red for decoration or for a non-destructive state. A failed key is red; a destructive action is red; nothing else is.
Don't use Brand Red beyond the wordmark mark and the app icon.
Don't set body text or a primary button in Carbon Purple.
Don't add paper grain, extra textures or decorative stripes to a working screen. The stamp's ink-wear mask is the one allowed texture.
Don't round corners beyond 2px on controls or 3px on stamps; no pill-shaped buttons.
Don't set display type in a system face. Barlow Condensed is the display face; the fallbacks exist only for a missing font.
Don't load remote fonts, icons or images. Every face and mark is bundled, and the renderer's CSP is `default-src 'self'`.
Don't use a glyph icon to carry meaning. Words, rules and stamps carry it.
